title: Microsoft Teams Rooms on Android: call quality feedback surveys after meetings
summary: The briefing passes: the rollout, default, Teams Rooms licensing and survey control are supported by Microsoft's notice and documentation. The checklist's device-update check has no corresponding controls-table row; remove that checklist step to keep the two consistent.

claims.claim: Microsoft is introducing call quality feedback surveys for Teams Rooms on Android.
claims.quote: Microsoft Teams is introducing call quality feedback (CQF) surveys for Microsoft Teams Rooms on Android.

claims.claim: Users are shown the surveys periodically.
claims.quote: Users will periodically see a call quality feedback survey after meetings end on Teams Rooms on Android devices.

claims.claim: The surveys appear after meetings end.
claims.quote: Users will periodically see a call quality feedback survey after meetings end on Teams Rooms on Android devices.

claims.claim: Users can rate their calls and meetings.
claims.quote: Users can now rate the quality of their calls and meetings

claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented a new identity, permission or sign-in requirement for these surveys.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams Rooms Android call quality feedback surveys identity permission sign-in requirements; read the Rooms release notes, Teams feedback guidance and feedback policies; security search results describe existing room-account requirements, not a new survey requirement.

claims.claim: The notice describes no action taken on the tenant's behalf.
claims.quote: Feedback will be used by Microsoft to improve Teams products and services.

claims.claim: The release notes warn that features can become available on particular device makes and models later than Microsoft's release.
claims.quote: There can be a delay between when features are released by Microsoft and when they become available on a device make and model.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance controls; controls[0].scope
claims.claim: Cloud Policy policies apply to user objects.
claims.quote: Policies only apply to user objects.

claims.claim: The user objects must be present in Microsoft Entra ID.
claims.quote: User objects must be present in Microsoft Entra ID and have a supported license assigned.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: Cloud Policy requires the user objects to have a supported licence assigned.
claims.quote: User objects must be present in Microsoft Entra ID and have a supported license assigned.

claims.claim: Cloud Policy supports applying policies through Microsoft Entra groups.
claims.quote: Cloud Policy Service supports the use of Microsoft Entra groups ... Policies only apply to user objects.

claims.claim: The survey control is reached in Microsoft 365 Apps admin center via Customization > Policy Management > Policy configurations > Create > Start with the basics > Choose the scope > Configure Settings > Allow users to receive and respond to in-product surveys from Microsoft.
claims.quote: Under Customization, select Policy Management. ... On the Policy configurations page, select Create. ... Start with the basics ... Choose the scope ... On the Configure Settings page, select the policies that you want to include in the policy configuration.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn documents no PowerShell, Graph or other API for these Cloud Policy policy configurations.
claims.quote: Searched: Cloud Policy policy configurations API PowerShell; Microsoft 365 Apps Cloud Policy configuration create update Graph beta API PowerShell surveys. Read overview-cloud-policy and feedback-manage; Set-CsTeamsFeedbackPolicy manages a separate Teams policy, not Cloud Policy configurations.

claims.claim: The feedback policies page lists Teams Rooms as supporting in-product surveys and documents a policy controlling whether those surveys appear.
claims.quote: | Teams Rooms | Yes | Yes | Yes | No | ... Allow users to receive and respond to in-product surveys from Microsoft | Controls whether surveys appear within product.

claims.claim: For the survey policy, Not Configured has the same effect as Enabled.
claims.quote: When the following policies are set to Not Configured, it has the same effect as if you set the policies to Enabled.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Disabling the documented in-product survey policy suppresses surveys rather than leaving them enabled or unconfigured.
claims.quote: Allow users to receive and respond to in-product surveys from Microsoft | Controls whether surveys appear within product.

claims.claim: Applied feedback-policy changes can take a few hours to reach clients.
claims.quote: After you apply policies, it can take a few hours for the client applications to update.

claims.claim: The Call Quality Feedback release-note entry does not describe how room accounts are targeted with feedback policies.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams Rooms Android call quality feedback surveys Cloud Policy API PowerShell licensing identity. Read the Android CQF release entry and its linked feedback-manage page; the entry links feedback policies but supplies no room-account targeting procedure.

claims.claim: The checklist's instruction to check device update status is represented in the controls table.
claims.quote: Check device update status in the Teams Rooms Pro Management portal under Rooms > device > Updates ... Whether Teams Rooms devices show in-product surveys, including call quality feedback prompts
claims.fix: Remove the At rollout bullet beginning 'Check device update status in the Teams Rooms Pro Management portal'. The device-update control has no row in the controls table; do not add a row as part of this correction.

claims.claim: MC1490912 does not identify who in the tenant can see individual survey responses.
claims.quote: Feedback will be used by Microsoft to improve Teams products and services.
